from_quote: The citizens of the State of New York have received yesterday, from Cato (an ally oi Pompey, no doubt), an introductory discourse on the appearance of the new system
rationale: The paragraph names Cato and his "introductory discourse" to the citizens of New York; Cato 1 appeared in the New York Journal on September 27, 1787, and this essay in the Daily Advertiser on October 1, 1787.

from_quote: as will promote our welfare and be justified by reason and truth.
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks Cato's closing promise of observations that "will promote our welfare and be justified by reason and truth" (Cato wrote "your welfare").
to_quote: welfare and be justified by reason and truth

from_quote: because you will admit that something must be done, adopt anything.
rationale: The paragraph quotes Cato's words in quotation marks ("Do not ... because you will admit that something must be done, adopt anything"), and later his "Teach the members of the Convention" passage, both from this paragraph of Cato 1.
to_quote: because you admit that something must be done, adopt anything

from_quote: He advises us to attach ourselves to measures, and not to men.
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks, as Cato's advice, Cato's words "Attach yourselves to measures, not to men".
to_quote: Attach yourselves to measures, not to men.
